legal.headline: Legal Notes by Arvind Datar: Indefinite is not perpetual
legal.hook: Legal Notes by Arvind Datar: Indefinite is not perpetual
legal.summary: A contract will not be treated as perpetual unless there are clear words to indicate the intention of perpetuity.
legal.contextNote: Bar & Bench reports a recent judgment clarifying that a contract cannot be deemed perpetual absent explicit language indicating an intention to create an endless term. The decision interprets the Indian Contract Act, 1872, applying Section 27 (restraint of trade) and the principle that contracts must have a definite duration unless expressly stated otherwise. No specific precedent is cited in the article; the ruling aligns with earlier Supreme Court pronouncements that implied perpetual obligations are unenforceable.

legal.contextNote: An arbitration-law development before Supreme Court. (1) Diarise the s.34 challenge window — three months from receipt of the award, extendable by 30 days — for any award a client holds or faces. (2) Where assets may be dissipated, s.9 interim relief is available before and during the proceedings. (3) Check the arbitration clause's seat and institutional rules, which decide the supervising court and the appointment route.
